transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-08-22 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Rahul (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood DevEx); Alex (CTO), Maya (Platform/SRE), Ben (Sr Eng), Sofia (Security)

Summary:
Quickwalk: SDK bootstrap focusing on env setup (Python + TS), KMS integration options (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed), and VPC/private deployment considerations. Agreed to run a small pilot with a perf run; action items assigned.

Topics covered:
- SDK install and token management (rotate/local CI secrets)
- KMS integrations (AWS KMS vs customer HSM) and key policies
- VPC/private deployment patterns and DNS/workload routing
- Quick validation: hello-world call, streaming, and error handling
- Questions around data residency, logs, and SOC2 artifacts

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie (AE): Alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um we'll do a short run through — 45ish minutes — walk through the SDKs, auth, and then Rahul will jump in on KMS and VPC glue.
[00:23] Alex (CTO): Sounds good. We want to validate we can keep PII in our VPC and control keys — so KMS is the main ask.
[00:38] Rahul (SE): Yep, totally. We'll show both patterns: Redwood-managed keys with customer CMEK—sorry, customer's KMS, and the private deployment pattern where you run Redwood Private in a VPC.
[00:55] Maya (Platform): Quick note — our stack is mostly k8s on EKS, use Terraform for infra. We're running HashiCorp Vault for some secrets.
[01:12] Priya (DevEx): Great, we'll point at the sample Terraform modules and the SDK snippets for Python and TypeScript. I have a repo link I'll drop in the notes.
[01:30] Ben (Sr Eng): Do you have a node example that shows streaming tokens? Our UX needs partial renders.
[01:45] Rahul (SE): Yes — both SDKs support streaming. For TS we show readable streams; Python uses async iterators. There are small differences for chunk size, but you can wire them straight into the UI.
[02:05] Sofia (Security): Also please clarify audit logs — if we use Redwood Hosted, do logs leave our VPC? We need to ensure only metadata leaves and content doesn't persist.
[02:25] Jamie (AE): Good Q. We'll pull the security doc. Short answer: hosted keeps request/response for X days for debugging; you can opt-in to tighter retention or use Private to keep everything inside. We'll share the SOC2 and logs page.
[02:47] Alex (CTO): What's the path for a dev to get from a PoC to Dedicated capacity? We need predictable latency.
[03:05] Jamie (AE): We do reserved pools under Redwood Dedicated — commit levels and SLA. Rahul can show perf tradeoffs between dedicated and hosted with batching configs.

[03:25] Rahul (SE): Ok jumping into the code — first the quickstart in Python.
[03:30] Rahul (SE): (screen) pip install redwood-client — then set REDWOOD_API_KEY as a secret, either in your CI or Vault. Example: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); resp = client.generate("summarize..." )
[03:55] Ben (Sr Eng): We usually rotate keys with Vault dynamic creds. Is token rotation compatible?
[04:10] Priya (DevEx): Yes. We recommend short-lived tokens and token rotation; our SDK respects 401s and will prompt for reauth flows. We also have a token refresh helper for server-side apps.
[04:28] Alex (CTO): For KMS — can Redwood call our KMS directly or do we need to provide encrypted keys to Redwood?
[04:45] Rahul (SE): Two modes. 1) Customer-managed keys (CMEK): you provide a key policy + we use API calls to wrap/unwrap — requires cross-account role. 2) Private deployment: you host the inference plane in your VPC and Redwood control plane just for management, keys never leave your environment. There's also a hybrid where we use envelope encryption with your KMS.
[05:12] Sofia (Security): If we do Redwood-managed but with CMEK, where are the unwrapped plaintext keys processed?
[05:25] Rahul (SE): The unwrapped material is only in the runtime memory ephemeral; we don't persist plaintext. But for the highest assurance the private on-prem/VPC path is recommended. We'll send the KMS flow diagram.
[05:45] Jamie (AE): I'll drop the security diagram and the KMS handoff doc after the call.

[06:05] Rahul (SE): Now VPC routing — two options: full private (control plane isolated) or peered via VPC peering or PrivateLink. For EKS we usually set up an interface endpoint and route to the inference nodes. DNS needs split-horizon so you resolve internal endpoints.
[06:35] Maya (Platform): Do you have terraform modules for the VPC endpoints?
[06:42] Rahul (SE): Yes, sample module in the repo. We'll push a variant for EKS + alb + nodegroup.
[07:00] Ben (Sr Eng): Any changes we need to make to our egress rules? We prefer deny-all by default.
[07:12] Rahul (SE): You need egress to the Redwood control plane (if using managed) for orchestration; for private, runtime nodes don't need outbound internet if you host all images in your registry. We'll detail minimal endpoints.
[07:35] Alex (CTO): Let's talk perf — what's latency with 1k token context on a gpus-backed Dedicated pool?
[07:50] Rahul (SE): Typical 90p latency depends on model + quantization. For comparable open models on our x1-like nodes you'd see 200-300ms per token in a single-stream scenario; with batching optimized you can trade latency for throughput. We can run a mini benchmark on your prompt set.
[08:15] Ben (Sr Eng): And cost math — is batching auto or manual?
[08:25] Jamie (AE): Redwood Optimize suggests batching rules and you can set max latency SLOs. The platform auto-batches within those constraints, but you can pin manual batch sizes for critical routes.

[08:50] Priya (DevEx): Back to SDK — here's an example TS snippet for streaming: (reads) const stream = client.chat.stream(...); stream.on('data', chunk => { /* render partial */ }); stream.on('end', () => {...});
[09:15] Ben (Sr Eng): Any gotchas for WebSocket vs SSE?
[09:22] Rahul (SE): SSE is simpler and works in most browsers; websockets are supported for two-way low-latency. We'll include sample layers for both.

[09:45] Alex (CTO): For auditability, can we route logs to our Splunk?
[09:52] Jamie (AE): Yes — we support forwarding webhooks to SIEM or pushing to S3 then you can ingest. For Private you can choose entirely internal sinks.
[10:10] Sofia (Security): What's the retention policy by default?
[10:16] Jamie (AE): Hosted default is 30 days for request content; metadata longer. We have an option to reduce to 0 for sensitive workloads but that limits debug capabilities. Private mode gives you full control.

[10:40] Rahul (SE): Quick demo — sandbox. I'll run a hello-world python call and show the console.
[10:50] Rahul (SE): (types) run sample script... ok, response streaming in — you can see partial tokens and headers in the trace panel.
[11:15] Maya (Platform): The console trace view looks like it shows token-level cost — can that be exported?
[11:22] Priya (DevEx): Yes CSV export per token and per-route. Useful for chargeback.
[11:35] Ben (Sr Eng): Any gotchas with CORS if we call directly from browser?
[11:42] Rahul (SE): We recommend server-side calls or token exchange via ephemeral tokens. Direct browser calls are possible with short-lived keys but you must ensure proper rate limiting.

[12:05] Alex (CTO): For pilot scope I want: 1) integrate SDK with our staging, 2) KMS envelope test, 3) perf run with 500 prompt samples. How long till results?
[12:20] Jamie (AE): We estimate 7–10 business days if we get sample prompts and test creds. Rahul will run the perf and return numbers.
[12:35] Rahul (SE): I'll need samples and a sandbox account. Priya will provide a starter repo.
[12:50] Sofia (Security): Please include the exact dataflow diagram for CMEK — I need to show legal.
[12:58] Rahul (SE): Yep, we'll add the diagram and the change log.

[13:10] (brief cross-talk, small audio cut)
[13:45] Jamie (AE): Ok let's summarize next steps — Jamie to send pricing and docs; Rahul to run bench; Priya to push starter repo; Sofia to confirm KMS vendor.
[14:05] Alex (CTO): Also please list any prerequisites so our infra team can prep.
[14:12] Priya (DevEx): We'll send a checklist: terraform modules, VPC rules, token rotation docs, sample k8s manifests.
[14:30] Ben (Sr Eng): One more — what's the rollback plan if model upgrade regresses?
[14:38] Rahul (SE): Console supports canary rollouts and pinned versioning. We keep model versions and can auto-fallback. We'll show an example rollout json.
[14:55] Sofia (Security): Thanks, that's helpful.
[15:05] Jamie (AE): Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with attachments: pricing worksheet, KMS whitepaper, SOC2 pack, starter repo link (https://git.redwood.ai/polarismed-sdk-starter) and the sample terraform module link.
[15:30] Alex (CTO): Thanks, talk soon.
[15:37] (call ends)
